thread:
li: Weird spike during the 03:00 UTC rollout window. Multiple GPU nodes failing attach with io timeouts, traced to nvme trim/flush activity on nvme0.
infra-bot: alert: nvme_trim_pause_seconds > 2.0 on gnode-512, gnode-513 (rules/nvme_trim_hang)
noah: saw the same. dmesg from gnode-512: 
```nvm0: firmware v2.3.9 applied 2026-02-10
nvme0: trim_flush: start
blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456789
blocking for 2.4s
```
emma: blocking trim/flush causing controller to stall, takes down active IO for short bursts. our attach path waits on block device leading to pod attach failures (~15-25s).
carla: metrics: read_iops dropped from 950->40 during stall, attach_timeout_count +12 in 5m window.
li: did we push firmware recently? the v2.3.9 rollout was last week to all regional fleets.
noah: yes, the firmware rollout was via image-job FW-UP-2026-02 and targeted nodes in batch. some nodes on v2.3.8 are fine.
sre-manager: immediate ask: can we quarantine affected nodes and rollback firmware on them? Also need a mitigation to keep janitor/scrub from running concurrent heavy IO.
emma: short-term mitigations:
  - set node label `nvme.trim.disabled=true` to skip scheduled trim jobs via janitor selector
  - suspend full scrubs on nodes with trim_pause_rate > 0.5%
  - add pre-attach check: avoid nodes with active trim_flush in last 10s
noah: quick commands to label nodes (draft):
```
kubectl label node gnode-512 nvme.trim.disabled=true --overwrite
kubectl label node gnode-513 nvme.trim.disabled=true --overwrite
```
carla: rolling rollback plan: identify nodes with firmware v2.3.9 and move them to maintenance, then re-image to v2.3.8. This will take ~20-30m per node if we drain GPUs.
li: can we avoid draining GPUs by using off-host reflash? riskier. prefer scheduled maintenance.
sre-manager: we should canary rollback in one region with low traffic (ap-south1) and observe. Do not mass rollback global fleet yet.
noah: proposed temporary patch to janitor cron: add `--skip-trim` flag when node label is set, and add token-bucket cap of 40MB/s for trim-related ops.
emma: also add alert: if attach_timeout_rate > 0.01 trigger urgent paging to infra oncall.
carla: operational note: disabling trim increases stale block map size and can affect future scrubs. need to record this state in node metadata and run a deferred trim in a maintenance window.
li: assigned: INFRA-2901 to track rollback + mitigation. I'll own rollback canary.
noah: timeline: canary rollback tonight at 22:30 UTC for 2 nodes in ap-south1, monitor for 1h. If attach failures fall < baseline, expand.
emma: also scheduling janitor change: add `--skip-trim-label` selector and deploy as 1-2 line change in infra repo, canary to staging first.
carla: I ran a quick wear calc: disabling trims briefly increases write amplification a bit (reclaim deferred) but rolling rollback likely reduces controller stalling which is better for overall device longevity.
sre-manager: decision: canary rollback + label-based scrub skip + alert changes. No immediate fleet-wide rollback unless canary proves positive.
li: I'll open a follow-up to track deferred trims and a maintenance schedule.
noah: logs/queries I'll paste in INFRA-2901. For visibility: attach failures correlate with firmware commit id sha:fa12bc.
emma: snippet for pre-attach check patch (pseudocode):
```
if node.labels['nvme.trim.disabled'] == 'true' or node.metrics.trim_pause_recent > 0.5%:
  avoid_node_for_attach()
```
carla: tagging storage team and schedulers. Also notify procurement for possible firmware vendor alert if more nodes affected.
sre-manager: good. @li run canary, @noah prepare rollback scripts, @emma submit janitor patch PR, @carla coordinate maintenance window. I'll be on call during canary.
li: canary scheduled. posting back with results in this thread.
infra-bot: ticket INFRA-2901 created and linked to alert.
li: thanks everyone. keeping this thread as single source. we'll reconvene if regressions occur.
